summary: Rory Mackenzie specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed doctoral studies under Peter Harvey and served as a teacher at International Christian College.

An Indologist, Rosalind Lefeber earned her doctorate at the University of Toronto under supervisors Bimal Krishna Matilal and Ronald Morton Smith, and was also taught by Daniel H. H. Ingalls. Her affiliation with the University of Toronto is attested in 2007.

Rosalind O'Hanlon works in Indology and history/archaeology, having earned her PhD at SOAS University of London (~1978–1983). She was an Emeritus Fellow at Clare College, Cambridge (~1982–2006), Professor at Oxford (~2006–2021), and became a British Academy Fellow in 2020.

Rosan Ikeda studied Buddhist studies at Komazawa University (1960–1964, ~1964–1969). He held several posts there, including assistant (1969), lecturer (1972), associate professor (1977), and professor (1983–2012), and became head of the Soto Zen Research Center in 2009.

Indologist and linguist Rosane Rocher earned an MA from Université libre de Bruxelles (~1955–1959) and studied under Ludo Rocher (~1957–1965). She worked at the National Fund for Scientific Research (1961–1970) before becoming a professor at the University of Pennsylvania (1970).

Rosemarie Fuchs is an active figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under Katia Holmes and traditional teacher Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche (attested 2000), and served as a member of the Marpa Translation Committee (attested 2000).

Rosemarie Lühr earned her doctorate under Karl Hoffmann at Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1970–1977) and completed her habilitation at Regensburg (~1977–1984). She held professorships at Giessen (1990–1994) and Jena (1994–2013), and later became honorary professor at Humboldt University of Berlin (2013).
Rosemary Radford Ruether worked in religious studies, studying at Claremont School of Theology from ~1960 to 1965. She held an academic post at Howard University from ~1965 to 1975.

Rosina Pastore specializes in Indology and religious studies, completing her PhD at the University of Lausanne under Maya Burger and co-supervisor Stefania Cavaliere. She served as an assistant at Lausanne and is an affiliated researcher at Ghent University (attested 2026).

Ross Bolleter earned a bachelor's degree at the University of Western Australia (~1964–1967), studying under David Tunley, and received traditional training under John Tarrant and Robert Baker Aitken (1982–1992). He served as a Zen Buddhist teacher at the Zen Group of Western Australia (~1991–2023).

Roy Rappaport earned his doctorate from Columbia University (~1959–1966). In the field of religious studies and anthropology, he served as Chair of Anthropology at the University of Michigan (~1965–1997) and was president of the American Anthropological Association (~1987–1989).

Roy Tzohar works in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tel Aviv University (~1997–2004) and Columbia University (~2004–2011) for his PhD under Gary A. Tubb, later holding a post at Tel Aviv University (~2012).

Roy W. Perrett studied at the University of Canterbury (~1970–1975) and the University of Otago (~1980–1984). Working in philosophy and Indology, he held posts at Massey University (~1987–2002), the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (~2002–2006), and the University of Melbourne (~2006–2011).

Royall Tyler studied at Harvard (BA 1954–1957) and Columbia (MA ~1963, PhD under Donald Keene ~1963–1977). He taught at Ohio State, Wisconsin-Madison, and Oslo, headed the Japan Centre at Australian National University (1990–2000), and was a visiting professor at Harvard (2001–2002).
Royce Wiles is a scholar of Indology who earned his PhD at the Australian National University by 2000 and subsequently held an academic post there.

Habito studied at Ateneo de Manila, the University of Tokyo (under Akira Hirakawa and Jikido Takasaki), and Sophia University. He held posts at Sophia University (~1975–1989), Ryukoku University, and Southern Methodist University (from 1989), and founded the Maria Kannon Zen Center.
Rudolf Geiger studied at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg from ~1913 to 1917 and later held a post at the University of Munich from ~1937 to 1958.

Rudolf Haym studied at Köllnisches Gymnasium (1834), Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1839), and Frederick William University Berlin (~1841–1843). Working in philosophy and history/archaeology, he held a post at the University of Halle-Wittenberg in 1868.

Rudolf Kaschewsky studied at the University of Bonn (~1959–1963) and University of Cologne (~1963–1967). Working in Tibetology, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies, he served as an academic official at Bonn (1974–2004) and taught Tibetan at Goethe University Frankfurt.
Rudolf Lange worked in Japanology and linguistics. He held academic posts at the University of Tokyo from ~1874 to 1881 and at Humboldt University of Berlin from ~1887 to 1923.
